EXECUTIVE ORDER 10444
Amendment  op E xecutive  O rder N o.
88091  op J une  28, 1941, Establishing
the G ood C onduct  M edal, as
Amended by  E xecutive  O rder N o.
93233  of M arch 31, 1943
Executive Order No. 8809 of June 28, 
1941, establishing the Good Conduct 
Medal, as amended by Executive Order 
No. 9323 of March 31, 1943, is hereby 
further amended to read as follows:
“By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States and 
as Commander in Chief of the Armed 
Forces of the United States, it is ordered 
as follows:
“There is hereby established the Good 
Conduct Medal, which shall include 
suitable appurtenances. Such medal 
may be ^warded for exemplary behavior, 
efficiency, and fidelity, under such regu­
lations as the Secretary of the Army and 
the Secretary of the Air Force shall 
severally prescribe, to those enlisted 
men of the Army of the United States 
and the'United States Air Force who on 
or after August 27, 1940, had or shall 
have honorably completed three years of 
active Federal military service, or who 
after December 7, 1941, have or shall- 
have honorably served one year of active 
Federal military service while the 
United States is at war, or who at the 
time of the termination of their active 
Federal military service have not previ­
ously been awarded a Good Conduct 
Medal and have completed a period of 
honorable service of less than three 
years if any part of that period of service 
has been performed after June 27, 1950: 
Provided,  that no persons, except per­
sons ¡separated from the active Federal 
military service by reason of physical 
disability incurred in line of duty, shall, 
be awarded such medal for a period of 
service of less than one year.”

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order restates Executive Order 8809 (as amended by 9323) as one paragraph establishing the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, with eligibility by three years of service from August 27, 1940, one year of wartime service after December 7, 1941, or shorter honorable service after June 27, 1950, and a proviso against awards for under one year except for service-incurred disability. Executive Order 14085 section 2 (87 FR 60541; the order states no later effective date, so the signing date October 3, 2022 is used) amended that restated text: (a) striking "men" and inserting "members"; (b) inserting "and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of the United States Space Force," after "August 27, 1940,"; (c) the same insertion after "December 7, 1941,"; and (d) inserting ", and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of the United States Space Force" after "June 27, 1950". The amendment widens the persons and service covered and does not end the clause. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, the U.S. Code note still prints it as amended, and the order cites no authority statute that could lapse, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (18 FR 2069, signed 1953-04-10; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt). It further amends Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 of March 31, 1943, to read as one restated paragraph, issued under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces (no authority statute is cited). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or who after December 7, 1941 served one year of active Federal military service while the United States is at war, or who at termination of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one, except persons separated by reason of physical disability incurred in line of duty, receives the medal for service of less than one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit, the note at 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 that prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085, sec. 2 (Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541), with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 0 hits. A search of the held texts for the number 10444 finds the order's own copies, Executive Order 14085, Executive Order 10445 (which makes conforming editorial notes in the Army and Air Force regulations in 32 CFR parts 578 and 878 and does not amend this order), the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification of EO 8809 (which records that EO 8809 was amended and restated by this order), and Federal Register pages of 1954 and 1967 whose authority citations name this order; none revokes or supersedes it. The one later amendment, Executive Order 14085 section 2 (87 FR 60541), is recorded as a later event with its before and after wording. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Item 1 authorizes the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy and the Air Force to issue a citation in the name of the President to any organization, detachment, installation, ship, aircraft or other unit for outstanding performance in action on or after October 16, 1941 (Navy or Marine Corps) or December 7, 1941 (Army or Air Force), and to units of co-belligerent forces. Executive Order 13286 section 74 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) added a new section 5 that lets the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating exercise the same authority for the Coast Guard as the Secretary of the Navy has for the Navy and Marine Corps (before: no Coast Guard provision; after: new section 5). Executive Order 14085 section 3 (87 FR 60542, effective on signing, October 3, 2022) amended paragraph 1 by inserting a Space Force case after the words or the Air Force (before: Army or Air Force only; after: the Space Force on or after December 20, 2019). Neither amendment ends the clause, and the Code note prints the order as amended, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Item 4 says that the order supersedes Executive Orders No. 9050 of February 6, 1942 and No. 9396 of November 22, 1943. That command was performed when the order took effect: it states no later effective date, so the signing date, January 10, 1957, is used. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note 'Supersedes: EO 9050, February 6, 1942; EO 9396, November 22, 1943' records the same effect. The clause supersedes earlier orders and creates no continuing duty, so it is exhausted by performance; the earlier orders' supersession is not undone. The order's other clauses continue.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10694 of January 10, 1957 (22 FR 253; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10694.txt, read in full) authorizes the Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force to issue citations in the name of the President to units for outstanding performance in action, sets out the insignia and ribbon rules, and supersedes Executive Orders 9050 and 9396. The held page text is interrupted by the issue's contents and masthead pages and by a running head and a page number, so the machine clauses (which cut item 2 across 7,690 characters of those pages) are replaced by an inventory override of the lead-in, item 1, items 2 and 3 (two spans each) and item 4. Own terms: no clause has an end date or ending condition; item 4 is a one-time supersession exhausted on issuance. Later instruments: Executive Order 13286 section 74 (official text in the packet, effective March 1, 2003 under section 92) added a section 5 for the Coast Guard, and Executive Order 14085 section 3 (official text in the packet, October 3, 2022) amended paragraph 1; both are recorded as later events on item 1. The packet's ACT:EO:10694>EO:12977 lead points to a source-ladder file containing the text of Executive Order 13286, and the held text of Executive Order 12977 does not mention this order, so it adds no instrument. Executive Order 13870 (May 9, 2019) (paragraph (d) of its awards section) refers to citations issued under this order as amended and changes nothing. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads 'Amended by: EO 13286, February 28, 2003 | Supersedes: EO 9050, February 6, 1942; EO 9396, November 22, 1943'; the catalog does not list Executive Order 14085, which the Code note and the held text of 14085 show. Current law: current-law:usc has 3 hits (the 10 U.S.C. ch. 57 note printing the order as amended and other Code notes), current-law:ecfr 0 hits. No search or held text revokes or supersedes the order.

EO 13286 section 74 and EO 14085 section 3 amend item 1 and do not end it.","independent_command_check":"Item 1 (authority to cite units), items 2 and 3 (insignia and ribbons) and item 4 (supersession) are independent; item 4's performance does not end the others, and the amendments touch only item 1.","savings_check":"Item 4 is a one-time supersession with no residual duty; no savings clause exists; the amendments are recorded as later events with before and after effect.","scope_check":"The corrected inventory has eight clauses (lead-in, item 1, items 2a and 2b, items 3a and 3b, item 4) covering every operative sentence between the authority recital and the signature; the intervening issue pages are not part of the order."}

Ex. Ord. No. 11145, Mar. 7, 1964, 29 F.R. 3189, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 11565, Oct. 13, 1970, 35 F.R. 16155, provided:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 establishes the Committee for the Preservation of the White House (members: the Director of the National Park Service as Chairman, the Curator, the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, the Chairman of the Commission of Fine Arts, the Director of the National Gallery of Art, the Chief Usher, and seven other members appointed by the President; members serve without compensation). Executive Order 11565 (October 13, 1970, effective on signing) substituted a new section 2 that is the same except that the seven other members became so many other members as the President may from time to time appoint (before: seven appointed members; after: such number as the President appoints). The substance of the membership rule changed in that respect only. Each biennial continuation order since 1975, listed as a later event with its signing date, continued the Committee without changing this provision; the latest, Executive Order 14354 (2025), continues it until September 30, 2027. The Committee is therefore in existence on 2026-10-14 and the clause is operative.

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11565
AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 11145 WITH RESPECT TO THE  
MEMBERSHIP OF THE COMMITTEE FOR THE PRESERVATION OF THE  
WHITE HOUSE
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United  
States, Executive Order No. 11145 1  of March 7,1964, “Providing for  
a Curator of the White House and Establishing a Committee for the  
Preservation of the White House,” is hereby amended by substituting  
the following for section 2:
“ Sec. 2. There is hereby established the Committee for the Preser­
vation of the White House, hereinafter referred to as the ‘Committee’.  
The Committee shall be composed of the Director of the National Park  
Service, the Curator of the White House, the Secretary of the Smith­
sonian Institution, the Chairman of the Commission of Fine Arts,  
the Director of the National Gallery of Art, the Chief Usher of the  
White House, and so many other members as the President may from  
time to time appoint. The Director of the National Park Service shall  
serve as Chairman of the Committee and shall designate an employee  
of that Service to act as Executive Secretary of the Committee. Mem­
bers of the Committee shall serve without compensation.”

Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
Under the provisions of Section 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee  
Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ), each advisory committee created by the Pres­
ident or any other officer of the Executive Branch and subject to the  
provisions of this Act— in existence on the effective date of the Act,  
January 5, 1973— will terminate on January 5, 1975, unless renewed  
by the President or other appropriate officer.
During the period elapsed since the Federal Advisory Committee Act  
was enacted, all Federal advisory committees subject to that Act have  
been thoroughly examined and reexamined to determine whether they  
should be continued, modifiedj abolished, or allowed to terminate. In  
that period, more than 300 Federal advisory committees have been  
abolished or allowed to terminate.
All advisory committees created by the President before the effective  
date of the Act and subject to the provisions of the Act have been care­
fully examined. I have determined that those listed in Section 1  of this  
Order should be continued until January 5, 1977, unless terminated  
sooner. I have also determined that the advisory committees listed in  
Section 2 of this Order, created after the effective date of the Federal  
Advisory Committee Act— expiring under the terms of that Act before  
January 5, 1977—should be continued until that date, unless terminated  
sooner.

‘‘Section 1. Establishment. (a) There is established the President’s National 
Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee, which shall be com-
posed of no more than 30 members. These members shall have particular 
knowledge and expertise in the fields of cybersecurity and of information 
and communications technology (ICT) and shall represent various elements 
of the Nation’s telecommunications industry. Members of the Committee 
shall be appointed by the President. 
(b) The President shall designate a Chair and Vice Chair from among 
the members of the Committee, each for a term of up to 2 years.’’ 
(b) by striking sections 2 and 3, and inserting in lieu thereof the following 
new sections 2 and 3: 
‘‘Sec. 2. Functions. (a) The Committee shall provide to the President, 
through the Secretary of Homeland Security, information and advice from 
the perspective of relevant cybersecurity, ICT, and telecommunications 
industries on information assurance, cybersecurity, and the ICT ecosystem 
with respect to national security and emergency preparedness (NS/EP) 
concerns. 
(b) The Committee shall provide information and advice to the President, 
through the Secretary of Homeland Security, regarding the feasibility of 
implementing specific measures to improve the resiliency and security 
of the digital and communications infrastructure of the United States. 
(c) The Committee shall provide technical information, advice, and rec-
ommendations as it relates to NS/EP policy issues concerning cybersecu-
rity, ICT, and telecommunications matters. 
(d) The Committee shall periodically report on matters in this section 
to the President, through the Secretary of Homeland Security. 
Sec. 3. Administration. (a) The heads of Executive agencies shall, to the 
extent permitted by law, provide the Committee with information con-
cerning NS/EP policy issues specific to cybersecurity, ICT, and tele-
communications matters in order for it to carry out its functions and 
mission. Information supplied to the Committee shall not, to the extent 
permitted by law, be available for public inspection. 
(b) Members of the Committee shall serve without any compensation 
for their work on the Committee. However, to the extent permitted by 
law, they shall be entitled to travel expenses, including per diem in 
lieu of subsistence. 
(c) Any expenses of the Committee shall, to the extent permitted by 
law, be paid from funds available to the Secretary of Homeland Security.’’ 
(c) by striking section 4, except subsection (b) thereof, and inserting imme-
diately preceding subsection (b) the following: 
‘‘Sec. 4. General. (a) Notwithstanding any other Executive Order, the func-
tions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as 
amended (5 U.S.C. App.), which are applicable to the Committee, except 
that of reporting annually to the Congress, shall be performed by the 
Secretary of Homeland Security, in accord with guidelines and procedures 
established by the Administrator of General Services.’’ 
Sec. 6. Executive Order 13231 of October 16, 2001, as amended, is further 
amended in section 3(a) by striking ‘‘The President shall designate from

current_predicate.legal_basis: The held original text of EO 11145 (29 FR 3189) states no end. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints the order, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 11565, as a note at 3 U.S.C. 110 (CURRENT:EO:11145#0), and the 5 U.S.C. 1013 note prints Executive Order 14354 (September 29, 2025), whose section 1(a) continues the Committee for the Preservation of the White House, Executive Order 11145 as amended, until September 30, 2027, a period that covers 2026-10-14; the held text of Executive Order 14354 is in the packet. current-law:ecfr has 0 hits and no held instrument revokes or supersedes the order. Checked through 2026-10-14.

Ex. Ord. No. 11145. Curator of White House; Committee for Preservation of White House
Ex. Ord. No. 11145, Mar. 7, 1964, 29 F.R. 3189, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 11565, Oct. 13, 1970, 35 F.R. 16155, provided:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(a) directs the Committee to report to the President and advise the Director of the National Park Service on the museum character of the principal corridor and public rooms, and to recommend articles, furnishings, decor and arrangements. Each biennial continuation order since 1975, listed as a later event with its signing date, continued the Committee without changing this provision; the latest, Executive Order 14354 (2025), continues it until September 30, 2027. The Committee's functions continue with it, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

Title 3—The President  
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11827 
Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
Under the provisions of Section 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee  
Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ), each advisory committee created by the Pres­
ident or any other officer of the Executive Branch and subject to the  
provisions of this Act— in existence on the effective date of the Act,  
January 5, 1973— will terminate on January 5, 1975, unless renewed  
by the President or other appropriate officer.
During the period elapsed since the Federal Advisory Committee Act  
was enacted, all Federal advisory committees subject to that Act have  
been thoroughly examined and reexamined to determine whether they  
should be continued, modifiedj abolished, or allowed to terminate. In  
that period, more than 300 Federal advisory committees have been  
abolished or allowed to terminate.
All advisory committees created by the President before the effective  
date of the Act and subject to the provisions of the Act have been care­
fully examined. I have determined that those listed in Section 1  of this  
Order should be continued until January 5, 1977, unless terminated  
sooner. I have also determined that the advisory committees listed in  
Section 2 of this Order, created after the effective date of the Federal  
Advisory Committee Act— expiring under the terms of that Act before  
January 5, 1977—should be continued until that date, unless terminated  
sooner.
NOW , THEREFORE, I, GERALD R. FORD, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of the United States of America,  
particularly by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, do hereby order as  
follows:

tinued until January 5, 1977,' unless otherwise sooner terminated—

Title 3—The President  
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11827 
Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
Under the provisions of Section 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee  
Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ), each advisory committee created by the Pres­
ident or any other officer of the Executive Branch and subject to the  
provisions of this Act— in existence on the effective date of the Act,  
January 5, 1973— will terminate on January 5, 1975, unless renewed  
by the President or other appropriate officer.
During the period elapsed since the Federal Advisory Committee Act  
was enacted, all Federal advisory committees subject to that Act have  
been thoroughly examined and reexamined to determine whether they  
should be continued, modifiedj abolished, or allowed to terminate. In  
that period, more than 300 Federal advisory committees have been  
abolished or allowed to terminate.
All advisory committees created by the President before the effective  
date of the Act and subject to the provisions of the Act have been care­
fully examined. I have determined that those listed in Section 1  of this  
Order should be continued until January 5, 1977, unless terminated  
sooner. I have also determined that the advisory committees listed in  
Section 2 of this Order, created after the effective date of the Federal  
Advisory Committee Act— expiring under the terms of that Act before  
January 5, 1977—should be continued until that date, unless terminated  
sooner.
NOW , THEREFORE, I, GERALD R. FORD, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of the United States of America,  
particularly by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, do hereby order as  
follows:
Section 1. The following-listed advisory committees are hereby con­
tinued until January 5, 1977,' unless otherwise sooner terminated—

‘‘Sec. 3. The National Infrastructure Advisory Council. The National Infra-
structure Advisory Council (NIAC), established on October 16, 2001, shall 
provide the President, through the Secretary of Homeland Security, with 
advice on the security and resilience of the critical infrastructure sectors 
and their functional systems, physical assets, and cyber networks. 
‘‘(a) Membership. The NIAC shall be composed of not more than 30 
members appointed by the President, taking appropriate account of the 
benefits of having members: 
‘‘(i) from the private sector, including individuals with experience in

ices organizations, institutions of higher education, environmental and 
climate resilience, and State, local, and tribal governments;

‘‘Unless otherwise determined by the President, no full-time officer or

‘‘(b) Functions of the NIAC. The NIAC shall meet periodically to: 
‘‘(i) enhance the partnership of the public and private sectors in securing

and provide reports on this issue to the President, through the Secretary

‘‘(ii) propose and develop ways to encourage private industry to perform 
periodic risk assessments and implement risk-reduction programs; 
‘‘(iii) monitor the development and operations of critical infrastructure 
sector coordinating councils and their information-sharing mechanisms 
and provide recommendations to the President, through the Secretary 
of Homeland Security, on how these organizations can best foster improved 
cooperation among the sectors, the Department of Homeland Security, 
and other Federal Government entities; 
‘‘(iv) report to the President through the Secretary of Homeland Security, 
who shall ensure appropriate coordination with the Assistant to the Presi-
dent for Homeland Security and Counterterrorism, the Assistant to the 
President for Economic Policy, and the Assistant to the President for 
National Security Affairs under the terms of this order; and 
‘‘(v) advise sector-specific agencies with critical infrastructure responsibil-
ities to include issues pertaining to sector and government coordinating 
councils and their information sharing mechanisms. 
‘‘In implementing this order, the NIAC shall not advise or otherwise 
act on matters pertaining to National Security and Emergency Preparedness 
(NS/EP) Communications and, with respect to any matters to which the 
NIAC is authorized by this order to provide advice or otherwise act on 
that may depend on or affect NS/EP Communications, shall coordinate with 
the National Security and Telecommunications Advisory Committee estab-
lished by Executive Order 12382 of September 13, 1982, as amended.’’.

Title 3—The President  
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11827 
Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
Under the provisions of Section 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee  
Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ), each advisory committee created by the Pres­
ident or any other officer of the Executive Branch and subject to the  
provisions of this Act— in existence on the effective date of the Act,  
January 5, 1973— will terminate on January 5, 1975, unless renewed  
by the President or other appropriate officer.
During the period elapsed since the Federal Advisory Committee Act  
was enacted, all Federal advisory committees subject to that Act have  
been thoroughly examined and reexamined to determine whether they  
should be continued, modifiedj abolished, or allowed to terminate. In  
that period, more than 300 Federal advisory committees have been  
abolished or allowed to terminate.
All advisory committees created by the President before the effective  
date of the Act and subject to the provisions of the Act have been care­
fully examined. I have determined that those listed in Section 1  of this  
Order should be continued until January 5, 1977, unless terminated  
sooner. I have also determined that the advisory committees listed in  
Section 2 of this Order, created after the effective date of the Federal  
Advisory Committee Act— expiring under the terms of that Act before  
January 5, 1977—should be continued until that date, unless terminated  
sooner.
NOW , THEREFORE, I, GERALD R. FORD, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of the United States of America,  
particularly by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, do hereby order as  
follows:

tinued until January 5, 1977,' unless otherwise sooner terminated—

Executive Order 12489 of September 28, 1984
Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
%
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America,
and in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee
Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Each advisory committee listed below is continued until September
30, 1985, unless terminated at a prior date by appropriate Executive order.
(a) Advisory Committee on Small and Minority Business Ownership; Execu­
tive Order No. 12190 (Small Business Administration).
(b) Committee for the Preservation of the White House; Executive Order No.
11145, as amended (Department of the Interior).
(c) Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health; Executive
Order No. 12196 (Department of Labor).
(d) President’s Commission on White House Fellowships; Executive Order No.
11183, as amended (Office of Personnel Management).
(e) President’s Committee on the Arts and the Humanities; Executive Order
No. 12367 (National Endowment for the Arts).
(f) President’s Committee on the International Labor Organization; Executive
Order No. 12216 (Department of Labor).
(g) President’s Committee on Mental Retardation; Executive Order No. 11776
(Department of Health and Human Services).
(h) President’s Comipittee on the National Medal of Science; Executive Order
No. 11287, as amended (National Science Foundation).
(i) President’s Council on Physical Fitness and Sports; Executive Order No.
12345, as amended (Department of Health and Human Services).
(j) President’s Economic Policy Advisory Board; Executive Order No. 12296
(Office of Policy Development).
(k) President’s Export Council; Executive Order No. 12131 (Department of
Commerce).
Sec. 2. The following advisory committee is continued until December 31,1984:
International Private Enterprise Task Force; Executive Order No. 12395
(Agency for International Development).

Executive Order 12974 of September 29, 1995
Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, and in accordance with the provisions
of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.), it
is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Each advisory committee listed below is continued until September
30, 1997.
(a) Committee for the Preservation of the White House; Executive Order
No. 11145, as amended (Department of the Interior).
(b) Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health; Executive
Order No. 12196, as amended (Department of Labor).
(c) National Partnership Council; Executive Order No. 12871 (Office of
Personnel Management).
(d) President’s Advisory Commission on Educational Excellence for His-
panic Americans; Executive Order No. 12900 (Department of Education).
(e) President’s Board of Advisors on Historically Black Colleges and Univer-
sities; Executive Order No. 12876 (Department of Education).
(f) President’s Commission on White House Fellowships; Executive Order
No. 11183, as amended (Office of Personnel Management).
(g) President’s Committee of Advisors on Science and Technology; Execu-
tive Order No. 12882, as amended (Office of Science and Technology Policy).
(h) President’s Committee on the Arts and the Humanities; Executive
Order No. 12367, as amended (National Endowment for the Arts).
(i) President’s Committee on the International Labor Organization; Execu-
tive Order No. 12216, as amended (Department of Labor).
(j) President’s Committee on Mental Retardation; Executive Order No.
11776, as amended (Department of Health and Human Services).
(k) President’s Committee on the National Medal of Science; Executive
Order No. 11287, as amended (National Science Foundation).
(l) President’s Council on Physical Fitness and Sports; Executive Order
No. 12345, as amended (Department of Health and Human Services).
(m) President’s Export Council; Executive Order No. 12131, as amended
(Department of Commerce).
(n) President’s National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee;
Executive Order No. 12382, as amended (Department of Defense).
(o) Trade and Environment Policy Advisory Committee; Executive Order
No. 12905 (Office of the United States Trade Representative).
Sec. 2. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive order, the
functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act that
are applicable to the committees listed in section 1 of this order, except
that of reporting annually to the Congress, shall be performed by the head
of the department or agency designated after each committee, in accordance
with the guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of
General Services.

Ex. Ord. No. 11145, Mar. 7, 1964, 29 F.R. 3189, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 11565, Oct. 13, 1970, 35 F.R. 16155, provided:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 directs each represented agency to furnish assistance consonant with law and the Department of the Interior to furnish administrative services to the Committee. Each biennial continuation order since 1975, listed as a later event with its signing date, continued the Committee without changing this provision; the latest, Executive Order 14354 (2025), continues it until September 30, 2027. The clause continues with the Committee and is operative on 2026-10-14.

Title 3—The President  
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11827 
Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
Under the provisions of Section 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee  
Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ), each advisory committee created by the Pres­
ident or any other officer of the Executive Branch and subject to the  
provisions of this Act— in existence on the effective date of the Act,  
January 5, 1973— will terminate on January 5, 1975, unless renewed  
by the President or other appropriate officer.
During the period elapsed since the Federal Advisory Committee Act  
was enacted, all Federal advisory committees subject to that Act have  
been thoroughly examined and reexamined to determine whether they  
should be continued, modifiedj abolished, or allowed to terminate. In  
that period, more than 300 Federal advisory committees have been  
abolished or allowed to terminate.
All advisory committees created by the President before the effective  
date of the Act and subject to the provisions of the Act have been care­
fully examined. I have determined that those listed in Section 1  of this  
Order should be continued until January 5, 1977, unless terminated  
sooner. I have also determined that the advisory committees listed in  
Section 2 of this Order, created after the effective date of the Federal  
Advisory Committee Act— expiring under the terms of that Act before  
January 5, 1977—should be continued until that date, unless terminated  
sooner.
NOW , THEREFORE, I, GERALD R. FORD, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of the United States of America,  
particularly by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, do hereby order as  
follows:
Section 1. The following-listed advisory committees are hereby con­
tinued until January 5, 1977,' unless otherwise sooner terminated—
(1) Citizens’ Advisory Committee on Environmental Quality— Exec­
utive Order No. 11472 of May 29, 1969, as amended ^(Council on  
Environmental Quality).

services organizations and institutions of higher learning, and State, local,

periodic risk assessments;

nating councils and their information sharing mechanisms and provide

Security on how these organizations can best foster improved cooperation 
among the sectors, the Department of Homeland Security, and other Federal

ities to include issues pertaining to sector and government coordinating 
councils and their information sharing mechanisms.’’

Executive Order 11145
PROVIDING FOR A CURATOR OF THE WHITE HOUSE AND ESTAB­
LISHING A COMMITTEE FOR THE PRESERVATION OF THE WHITE  
HOUSE
W HEREAS the White House, as the home of the highest elective 
officer of the United States
—symbolizes the American ideal of responsible self-government 
—is emblematic of our democracy and our national purpose
—has been intimately associated with the personal and social life 
of the Presidents of the United States and many of their official acts 
—occupies a particular place in the heart of every American citizen, 
and
W HEREAS certain historic rooms and entranceways in the White 
House
—possess great human interest and historic significance 
—traditionally have been open to visitors
—have provided pleasure and patriotic inspiration to millions of 
our citizens
—have come to be regarded as a public museum and the proud pos­
session of all Americans, and
W HEREAS the Congress by law (Act of September 22,1961), (75 
Stat. 586) has authorized the care and preservation of the historic 
and artistic contents of the Wliite House and has given the President 
certain responsibilities with regard thereto:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me as 
President of the United States, it is ordered as follows :
S ection  1. (a) There shall be in the White House a Curator of 
the White House. The Curator shall assist in the preservation and 
protection of the articles of furniture, fixtures, and decorative objects

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11145 of March 7, 1964 (29 FR 3189; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11145.txt, read in full; boundary verified) establishes a Curator of the White House (section 1) and the Committee for the Preservation of the White House (sections 2 to 4). The packet's seven machine clauses follow the order's sections and are accepted. Own terms: no section has an end date. Later instruments: Executive Order 11565 (October 13, 1970) substituted section 2, and the Office of the Federal Register catalog and the packet's actor texts show 27 advisory-committee continuation orders (26 are cited) from Executive Order 11827 (January 4, 1975) through Executive Order 14354 (September 29, 2025), each listing the Committee for the Preservation of the White House, Executive Order 11145 as amended, as continued until a stated date; each is recorded as a later event with its signing date. None of them amends the text of sections 1 to 4. The continuation order of September 29, 1989 (Executive Order 12692) is also held, but only as machine-located text whose page location is unconfirmed (location_confidence medium), so the claim kit does not accept it as a cited later-event source; it continued the Committee until September 30, 1991 and is superseded in effect by each later continuation, so it does not bear on the state on 2026-10-14. The catalog note lists Executive Order 12258 as dated December 28, 1980; the held text of Executive Order 12258 is dated December 31, 1980 and that date is used, as the catalog row's signing date also shows. The orders the packet lists as 'cited by number, no change provision located' (EO 12963, 13210, 13227, 13278, 13326, 13328, 14045, 14089, 13899) were checked: a search of their held texts for the Committee's name finds no continuation of it, and their sentences citing this order contain no amending, revoking or superseding verb. Current law: the Code note at 3 U.S.C. 110 prints the order as amended; the 5 U.S.C. 1013 note prints Executive Order 14354, which continues the Committee until September 30, 2027; eCFR 0 hits. The Curator clause rests on the same note; no held text abolishes the office.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No section has an own-terms end. Under the Federal Advisory Committee Act regime the Committee continued only for stated periods, and each period was renewed by a continuation order; the latest held order, Executive Order 14354, runs to September 30, 2027, so no expiry occurred before 2026-10-14. No held instrument revokes the order.","independent_command_check":"The Curator provision (section 1) is independent of the Committee provisions (sections 2 to 4); only the Committee depends on periodic continuation, and its continuation is shown to 2027-09-30.","savings_check":"No saving clause exists and no clause is exhausted by performance; the amendment of section 2 and each continuation are recorded as later events.","scope_check":"The seven packet clauses (sections 1(a), 1(b), 2, 3(a), 3(b), 3(c) and 4) cover every operative sentence from section 1 through section 4; the recitals and signature are outside them."}

The permits issued under Executive Order 8202 were preserved by section 4, which is a separate clause that continues.

Executive Order 10485 of September 3, 1953 (18 FR 5397; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10485.txt, read in full) designates the Federal Power Commission to receive applications for, and issue, Presidential permits for border facilities for electric energy and natural gas (section 1), lets the Chairman sign them (section 2), authorizes rules (section 3), preserves existing permits (section 4) and revokes Executive Order 8202 (section 5). The held page text of section 1(a)(3) is interrupted by the issue's contents and masthead pages; the packet's 10,449-character machine clause across them is replaced by two clauses and the other machine clauses are kept (inventory override of ten clauses). Own terms: no section has an end date. Later instruments: Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) (43 FR 4957, effective October 1, 1977 under its section 6) deleted section 2 and substituted the Secretary of Energy for the Federal Power Commission in sections 1, 3 and 4; it is recorded as a later event on sections 1, 1(b), 3 and 4 and as the end of section 2. The Office of the Federal Register note 'Revokes: EO 8202, July 13, 1939 | Amended by: EO 12038, February 3, 1978 | See: EO 11423, August 16, 1968; EO 12847, May 17, 1993; EO 13337, April 30, 2004' was reconciled: Executive Order 11423 (as amended by 12847), Executive Order 13337 and Executive Order 13867 (2019) each except facilities covered by Executive Order 10485 from the Secretary of State's permit designation, so they recite this order and neither amend, revoke nor supersede it (Executive Order 13867 revokes Executive Orders 13337 and 11423, not this order). The packet's lead 'cited by number, no change provision located: EO:11062' was not confirmed by a search of the held text of Executive Order 11062 for this order's number. Current law: current-law:usc has 6 hits (15 U.S.C. 717b note printing the order as amended by Executive Order 12038, and other Code references), current-law:ecfr has 10 hits (including 18 CFR 153.1 and 153.15), later-events:ofr_catalog 4 hits; no search shows an ending. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.

Sections 1, 3 and 4 have no end; the Code prints them as amended.","independent_command_check":"Section 1 (designation), section 2 (signing), section 3 (rules), section 4 (permit savings) and section 5 (revocation of Executive Order 8202) are independent; section 2's deletion and section 5's performance do not end the others.","savings_check":"Section 4 is the savings clause and continues; section 5's revocation does not affect permits saved by section 4.","scope_check":"The ten clauses cover every operative sentence from section 1 through section 5 (the recitals before 'NOW, THEREFORE', the signature and the issue pages between the two halves of section 1(a)(3) are outside them)."}

The revocation of Executive Order 8202 in section 5 was performed in 1953 and leaves no further duty.

“ Sec. 5.1. C iv il S ervice R e g u la tio n s . The Director, Office o f Personnel Man­

promote the efficiency o f the Government and the integrity o f the competitive 
service, and (4) a statement limiting the application o f the variation to the 
continuation o f the conditions which gave rise to it. Like variations shall be 
granted whenever like conditions exist. All such decisions and information 
concerning variations noted in the official record shall be published promptly

in a Federal Personnel Manual, Letter or Bulletin and in the Director’s next

“ Sec. 5.2. In v e s tig a tio n  a n d  E v a lu a tio n s . The Director may secure effective 
implementation o f the civil service laws, rules, and regulations, and all Execu­
tive orders imposing responsibilities on the Office by:
(a) Investigating the qualifications and suitability o f applicants for posi­
tions in the competitive service. The Director may require appointments to be 
made subject to investigation to enable the Director to determine, after ap­
pointment, that the requirements o f law or the civil service rules and regula­
tions have been met.
(b) Evaluating the effectiveness of: (1) personnel policies, programs, and 
operations o f Executive and other Federal agencies subject to the jurisdiction 
o f the Office, including their effectiveness with regard to merit selection and 
employee development; (2) agency compliance with and enforcement o f appli­
cable laws, rules, regulations and office directives; and (3) agency personnel 
management evaluation systems.
(c) Investigating, or directing an agency to investigate and report on, 
apparent violations o f applicable laws, rules, regulations, or directives requir­
ing corrective action, found in the course o f an evaluation.
(d) Requiring agencies to report, in a manner and at times as the Director 
may prescribe, personnel information the Director requests relating to civilian 
employees in the Executive branch o f the Government, as defined by Section 
311 o f the Civil Service Reform Act o f 1978, including positions and officers 
and employees in the competitive, excepted and Senior Executive services, 
whether permanent, career-conditional, temporary or emergency.
“ Sec. 5.3. E n forcem en t.
(a) The Director is authorized to ensure enforcement o f the civil service 
laws, rules, and regulations, and all applicable Executive orders, by:
( 1  ) Instructing an agency to separate or take other action against an 
employee serving an appointment subject to investigation when the Director 
finds that the employee is disqualified for Federal employment. Where the 
employee or the agency appeals the Director’s finding that a separation or 
other action is necessary, the Director may instruct the agency as to whether 
or not the employee should remain on duty and continue to receive pay 
pending adjudication o f the appeal: P ro v id e d , That when an agency separates 
or takes other action against an employee pursuant to thé Director’s instruc­
tions, and the Director, on the basis o f new evidence, subsequently reverses 
the initial decision as to the employee’s qualifications and suitability, the 
agency shall, upon request o f the Director, restore the employee to duty or 
otherwise reverse any action taken.
(2) Reporting the results o f evaluation or investigations to the head o f the 
agency concerned with instructions for any corrective action necessary, includ­
ing cancellation o f personnel actions where appropriate. The Director’s find­
ings resulting from evaluations or investigations are binding unless changed as 
a result o f agency evidence and arguments against them. If, during the course 
o f any evaluation or investigation under this Section, the Director finds evi­
dence o f matters which come >vithin the investigative and prosecutorial juris­
diction o f the Special Counsel o f the Merit Systems Protection Board, the 
Director shall refer this evidence to the Special Counsel for appropriate dispo­
sition.
(b) Whenever the Director issues specific instructions as to separation or 
other corrective action with regard to an employee, including cancellation o f a

Ex. Ord. No. 10982. Administration of Provisions of Chapter
Ex. Ord. No. 10982, Dec. 25, 1961, 27 F.R. 3, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 12107, Dec. 28, 1978, 44 F.R. 1055; Ex. Ord. No. 12748, Feb. 1, 1991, 56 F.R. 4521, provided:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2(b) designates the Civil Service Commission to perform the functions conferred on the President by section 6 of the act for allotments and assignments under section 5 of the act. Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404) substituted 'Office of Personnel Management' for 'Civil Service Commission' in the orders listed in its section 2-101, which includes this order (the list prints the number as '19982' in the scan, which is an OCR error for 10982 between 10973 and 11103) (before: Civil Service Commission; after: Office of Personnel Management). Executive Order 12748 section 5 (56 FR 4521; signed February 1, 1991) then amended section 2(b) 'to read as follows': the Office of Personnel Management performs the functions under 5 U.S.C. 5527 for allotments and assignments under 5 U.S.C. 5525 and advance payments to new appointees under 5 U.S.C. 5524a as added by section 107(a) of the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990 (before: allotments and assignments only, under the act's section 5; after: those plus advance payments to new appointees). Under its section 9(b) the order takes effect May 4, 1991 (the Office of Personnel Management may set an earlier date not before February 3, 1991; I found no such determination in the held texts, so the default date is used). The clause is amended, not ended, and the Code prints the amended text.

“ Sec. 5.3. E n forcem en t.
(a) The Director is authorized to ensure enforcement o f the civil service 
laws, rules, and regulations, and all applicable Executive orders, by:
( 1  ) Instructing an agency to separate or take other action against an 
employee serving an appointment subject to investigation when the Director 
finds that the employee is disqualified for Federal employment. Where the 
employee or the agency appeals the Director’s finding that a separation or 
other action is necessary, the Director may instruct the agency as to whether 
or not the employee should remain on duty and continue to receive pay 
pending adjudication o f the appeal: P ro v id e d , That when an agency separates 
or takes other action against an employee pursuant to thé Director’s instruc­
tions, and the Director, on the basis o f new evidence, subsequently reverses 
the initial decision as to the employee’s qualifications and suitability, the 
agency shall, upon request o f the Director, restore the employee to duty or 
otherwise reverse any action taken.
(2) Reporting the results o f evaluation or investigations to the head o f the 
agency concerned with instructions for any corrective action necessary, includ­
ing cancellation o f personnel actions where appropriate. The Director’s find­
ings resulting from evaluations or investigations are binding unless changed as 
a result o f agency evidence and arguments against them. If, during the course 
o f any evaluation or investigation under this Section, the Director finds evi­

other corrective action with regard to an employee, including cancellation o f a

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10982 of December 25, 1961 (27 FR 3; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10982.txt, read in full, characters 540-5550) administers the Act of September 26, 1961 on evacuation payments. The packet's ten machine clauses did not follow the sections; I read the whole order and replaced them by twelve clauses: the recital, 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 2(a), 2(b), the section 3 lead, 3(a), 3(b), 3(c), 4(a) and 4(b). Later instruments, both official texts held in the packet: Executive Order 12107 (December 28, 1978, effective January 1, 1979), which substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the listed orders, including this one (listed as '19982' in the scan, an OCR error), recorded on each clause that names the Commission; and Executive Order 12748 section 5 (signed February 1, 1991, effective May 4, 1991 by default under its section 9(b)), which restates section 2(b). The Code note at 5 U.S.C. 5527 prints the order as amended by both, and 28 CFR 0.154 and 5 CFR part 550 cite it. None of these ends any clause. Not held in the packet: the text of 5 U.S.C. 5522-5527 beyond the note and the later OPM regulations (5 CFR part 550 subpart D is held in the repo but not in the packet); the claim rests on the Code's printing of the order and the eCFR citations. research_rationale:
Executive Order 12318 of August 21, 1981 (46 FR 42833-42834; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12318.txt, read in full, location confidence high) transfers statistical policy functions from the Secretary of Commerce to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. The packet marked the own-text boundary unresolved and cut the order into 14 fragments; I read the whole order (heading, eight sections, signature and the effective date of August 23, 1981 in section 8) and replaced the inventory by nine clauses: the recital, sections 1, 2, 3, 4(a), 4(b), 5, 6 and sections 7 and 8 together. Section 4(a) (revocation of Executive Order 12013) and section 5 (transfer of records and funds) are one-time commands exhausted when the order took effect on 1981-08-23; the amendments in sections 1, 2, 3 and 4(b) are embodied in the Code's printing of Executive Orders 11541, 10253, 10033 and 11961 as amended by Executive Order 12318 (CURRENT:EO:12318#4, #3, #1, #2); sections 6 and 7 are open-ended and no held source ends them. Later instruments: Executive Order 12518 (June 3, 1985; official text in the packet) amended Executive Order 11961 outside section 4, and is recorded as a later event on section 4(b); the other orders amended (11541, 10253, 10033) show no later amendment in the Code notes beyond those predating 1981 and this order. A search of the held texts for the number 12318 finds the order's copies, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification, and Federal Register or CFR authority lines (15 CFR part 801; 15 CFR parts cite E.O. 11961 as amended by E.O. 12318) that treat the order as in force; none amends, revokes or supersedes it. Current law: current-law:usc 8 hits (the Code notes above), current-law:ecfr 1 hit (15 CFR part 801 authority line), later-events:ofr_catalog 0 hits.

Section 1. Amendments to Executive Order 9158. Executive Order 9158 
of May 11, 1942 (Air Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9242–A 
of September 11, 1942 (Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 
1942, to Provide that the Air Medal May Be Awarded to Persons Serving 
with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United States), 
is further amended as follows: 
(a) The first paragraph is amended— 
(i) by striking ‘‘Army and Navy’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Armed 
Forces’’; 
(ii) by striking ‘‘any person’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘those individ-
uals’’; 
(iii) by inserting ‘‘Air Force, Space Force,’’ after ‘‘Marine Corps,’’; and 
(iv) by striking ‘‘distinguishes, or has distinguished, himself’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘distinguish, or have distinguished, themselves’’. 
(b) The second paragraph is amended— 
(i) by amending the first sentence to read as follows: ‘‘The Air Medal 
and appurtenances thereto shall be of appropriate design approved by 
the Secretary of Defense and, under such regulations as the Secretaries 
of the military departments may prescribe, may be awarded by the Secretary 
of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, 
or the Secretary of Homeland Security with respect to the Coast Guard 
when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, or by such commanding 
officers of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, or 
Coast Guard as the said Secretaries may respectively designate.’’; and 
(ii) in the second sentence, by striking ‘‘his jurisdiction’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘the jurisdiction of the Navy’’. 
(c) The following new paragraph is added at the end of the Executive 
Order: ‘‘The regulations of the Secretaries of the military departments con-
cerned with respect to the award of the Air Medal shall, so far as practicable, 
be uniform and shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense.’’.

basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 14085 (signed 2022-10-03; 87 FR 60541; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14085.txt, read in full) amends six earlier orders on military decorations and awards (EO 9158 Air Medal, EO 8809 Good Conduct Medal, EO 10694 unit citations, EO 11046 Bronze Star Medal, EO 13830 delegation of authority to approve decorations, EO 11545 Defense Distinguished Service Medal) to cover the Space Force and to use gender-neutral and updated wording, and adds general provisions. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The packet inventory fragmented the sections, so it is replaced by eight clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition, and the order has no effective-date section, so each amendment took effect on signing. Later instruments: the held-text number search finds only the order's own Federal Register copies, the dossier chain lists no event, and the ofr_catalog search records no disposition note naming it. Current law: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints each amended order with a status line naming EO 14085: EO 9158 as amended by section 1, EO 8809 by section 2, EO 10694 by section 3 and EO 13830 by section 5 in notes under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57; EO 11046 as amended by section 4 in a note under 10 U.S.C. 7276; and EO 11545 as amended by section 6 in a note under 10 U.S.C. 1125. The 7276 note also records that paragraph (a) of section 4 could not be executed because EO 13286 had already made that identical amendment. The eCFR search has 0 hits. No section is found ended.

source.quote:
S ection  1. There is hereby established a Meritorious Service Medal, 
with acompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secre­
tary of a military department or the Secretary of Transportation with 
regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, 
or by such military commanders, or other appropriate officers as the 
Secretary concerned may designate, to any member of the armed forces 
of the United States, who has distinguished himself by outstanding 
meritorious achievement or service to the United States.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 establishes the Meritorious Service Medal, with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of a military department or by the Secretary of Transportation with regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, or by military commanders or other officers the Secretary concerned designates, to a member of the armed forces of the United States who has distinguished himself by outstanding meritorious achievement or service to the United States. Executive Order 12312 (July 2, 1981, effective on signing; the order states no later effective date) restated section 1 to permit the award also to a member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation (before: award to a member of the armed forces of the United States; after: or to a member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation). Executive Order 13286 section 61 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) further amended section 1 by striking the Secretary of Transportation and inserting the Secretary of Homeland Security. By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces of the United 
States, it is ordered as follows:

with acompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secre­
tary of a military department or the Secretary of Transportation with 
regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, 
or by such military commanders, or other appropriate officers as the

of the United States, who has distinguished himself by outstanding 
meritorious achievement or service to the United States.

regulations.

posthumously and, when so awarded, may be presented to such repre­

Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12109.txt, read in full) has two numbered sections. Section 1-101 designates the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for payment of comparability allowances to recruit and retain certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that, until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet inventory already separates the two sections, so no inventory correction was needed. THE PRESIDENT
[3195-01-M ]
Executive O rder 12109 Decem ber 28,1978
Federal Physicians Comparability Allowance
By the authority vested in me as President o f the United States o f America 
by Section 5948 o f Title 5 and Section 301 o f Title 3 o f the United States 
Code, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. The Director o f the Office o f Personnel Management is hereby 
designated and empowered to exercise, in consultation with the Director o f 
the Office o f Management and Budget, the authority o f the President under 
Section 5948 o f Title 5 o f the United States Code, to prescribe regulations, 
criteria, and conditions with regard to the payment o f comparability 
allowances to recruit and retain certain Federal physicians.
1-102. Until the Office o f Personnel Management is established (on or 
before January 1, 1979), pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978 (43 
FR 36037), the Civil Service Commission shall exercise the authority delegated 
under this Order to the Director o f the Office o f Personnel Management.
